title: Why Drainage Pipe Slope Matters
description: A common mistake in drainage installation is assuming that a steeper pipe slope drains water faster and better. In gravity-flow drainage systems, proper grade is critical for self-scouring velocity. If the slope is too flat, wastewater flows too slowly, allowing solids to settle and cause blockages. Conversely, if the slope is excessively steep, liquids drain rapidly while leaving solid waste behind on the pipe floor. For standard residential branch lines, maintaining the code-specified uniform slope—typically one-quarter inch drop per linear foot—ensures water and solids travel together efficiently without stranding debris.
